upstream_phase2l_b_summary.reason: only 7 folds / 7.0 effective validation observations after the horizon-length embargo (need >= 3 folds and >= 8.0 effective obs); the data cannot support a conclusive walk-forward test.

decision.reason: Phase 2L-B returned NEED_MORE_DATA for avg_dollar_volume_21d: only 7 non-overlapping walk-forward folds / 7.0 effective validation observations remained after the 63-session embargo, below the required 8.0. A ~40-name, ~3.04-year single-regime panel cannot support a conclusive out-of-sample test, so no model research and no model candidate are authorized; the disciplined next step is to acquire longer history and a broader point-in-time universe and retest.

current_panel.single_regime_note: The 2023-2026 export is essentially one extended bull regime; it lacks a sustained drawdown, so a 63-session signal cannot be tested out of a single regime.

data_gap_analysis.why_cannot_advance: NEED_MORE_DATA: after the horizon-length embargo the labeled calendar yields too few effectively independent validation observations to draw a conclusion. The panel is both too short (only one regime) and too narrow to support model research.

insufficient_folds_or_observations.explanation: Each non-overlapping validation block contributes ~validation_dates / horizon effective observations; with validation == horizon that is ~1 per fold, so clearing the floor requires materially more labeled history after the embargo than the current export provides.

expanded_dataset_requirements.note: avg_dollar_volume_21d is a price/volume liquidity feature, so fundamentals and analyst estimates are NOT required to retest it -- they are marked as future-phase data that only later, different hypotheses would need.

longer_price_history.description: Daily adjusted OHLCV reaching well before 2023, ideally a full market cycle including a sustained drawdown.
longer_price_history.leakage_risk: Corporate-action adjustment must use only data available as of each date; no future split/dividend adjustment applied to past prices.

broader_equity_universe.description: Materially more than the current ~40 mega-caps (toward the full S&P 500 / a broad liquid universe) to widen each cross-section and reduce long-leg ticker concentration.
broader_equity_universe.leakage_risk: Using today's index membership for history is survivorship bias; membership must be resolved as-of-date.

point_in_time_universe_membership.description: As-of-date index / universe constituent history so each date's cross-section uses only names that were members then.
point_in_time_universe_membership.leakage_risk: Back-applying current membership injects look-ahead and survivorship bias.

survivorship_bias_controls.description: Coverage of delisted / merged / renamed names over the history so the universe is not silently restricted to today's survivors.
survivorship_bias_controls.leakage_risk: Dropping delisted names inflates measured returns and any signal computed on the survivors.

liquidity_and_volume_history.description: Daily volume / dollar-volume history -- the direct input to avg_dollar_volume_21d -- across the longer span and broader universe.
liquidity_and_volume_history.leakage_risk: Features must stay trailing-only; volume spikes around events leak if not lagged.

benchmark_and_factor_data.description: Benchmark (SPY) and trailing risk series over the longer span for the beta / vol residualization controls.

sector_industry_classification.description: Point-in-time sector / industry tags to support neutralization and concentration control on the broader universe.
sector_industry_classification.leakage_risk: Applying current classification to history misclassifies reclassified names.

point_in_time_fundamentals.description: As-first-reported fundamentals with correct report-date lags.
point_in_time_fundamentals.leakage_risk: Restated figures and report-date misalignment are the dominant factor-research leakage source.
point_in_time_fundamentals.future_phase_note: Only needed by later fundamental / quality-value hypotheses, not by the liquidity candidate.

analyst_estimates_and_surprise.description: Point-in-time consensus estimates, revision timestamps, actual earnings dates and surprise.
analyst_estimates_and_surprise.leakage_risk: Using final/current consensus for a past date imports the future; earnings dates must be actual.
analyst_estimates_and_surprise.future_phase_note: Only needed by later revision / drift hypotheses.

minimum_viable_expanded_dataset.universe_breadth_note: Materially broader than the current ~40 names; the full liquid S&P 500 is the ideal target.
minimum_viable_expanded_dataset.survivorship_caveat_if_not_point_in_time: If true point-in-time membership cannot be sourced, the dataset must carry an explicit survivorship caveat and the retest must report results as survivorship-biased rather than treating them as clean.

target_validation_capacity.arithmetic_vs_regime_note: The session arithmetic above is only the minimum to clear the effective-observation gate; the binding constraint is REGIME COVERAGE. The 8-10 year target exists so the walk-forward spans more than one market regime, not merely to accumulate enough non-overlapping blocks.

data_quality_gates.description: Adjusted closes are internally consistent across the longer span; no discontinuities at the join between the old and the extended history.
data_quality_gates.check: Reconcile adjusted vs raw closes and verify total-return continuity.

data_quality_gates.description: Split and dividend adjustments are correct and applied with no look-ahead.
data_quality_gates.check: Spot-check known splits/dividends; confirm adjustments use only as-of-date information.

data_quality_gates.description: Trading-calendar gaps are handled explicitly; no silent forward-fill of prices across non-trading days.
data_quality_gates.check: Validate each name's date index against the exchange calendar.

data_quality_gates.description: Each ticker's history is continuous over its membership span with no unexplained gaps.
data_quality_gates.check: Flag names with interior gaps exceeding a tolerance.

data_quality_gates.description: Delisted / merged names are retained over their live span so the universe is not restricted to survivors.
data_quality_gates.check: Confirm delisted names appear up to their delist date and not after.
Assert uniqueness on the (date, ticker) key.

data_quality_gates.description: Forward labels are never forward-filled or imputed; a name with no genuine forward window is dropped, not filled.
data_quality_gates.check: Verify labels are computed only from realized future prices.

data_quality_gates.description: Universe membership is resolved point-in-time; today's membership is never back-applied to historical dates.
data_quality_gates.check: Confirm each date's cross-section uses as-of-date membership only.

implementation_options.data_scope: Extend the existing free end-of-day export backward (more years) and modestly widen the ticker list.
pros: No new spend; fastest to attempt; reuses the existing pipeline.
risks: No point-in-time membership (survivorship bias); free history depth and delisted-name coverage are limited and may not reach a full market cycle.

implementation_options.data_scope: Investigate broader free / low-cost end-of-day price and volume archives and a low-cost point-in-time constituent history.
pros: Wider universe and longer depth than the current export; low spend.
risks: Point-in-time constituent lists remain the scarce piece; coverage and adjustment quality must be validated against the data-quality gates before use.

implementation_options.data_scope: A paid point-in-time universe + price (+ optionally fundamentals) dataset with delisted-name coverage.
pros: Clean point-in-time membership and survivorship handling; the soundest basis for out-of-sample research.
risks: Cost and procurement lead time; decision deferred until the free / low-cost feasibility check (Phase 2K-E) is done.

preconditions: Expanded dataset assembled and passing every data_quality_gate.
Universe resolved point-in-time (or carrying an explicit survivorship caveat).
Coverage spans more than one market regime, including a sustained drawdown.
steps: Re-run the Phase 2K-B beta/vol-neutralized residual rank-IC test for avg_dollar_volume_21d on the expanded multi-regime panel.
Re-run the Phase 2K-C robustness battery (overlap-aware bootstrap, permutation null, leave-one-year-out, concentration, regime splits) on the expanded data.
Re-run the Phase 2L-A walk-forward design / Phase 2L-B model-free walk-forward validation, which now has enough folds and regimes to be conclusive.
Only if the model-free baseline passes walk-forward on multi-regime data may a later, separately gated phase design a simple single-feature candidate under the model-candidate gate.
research_retest_plan.still_no_model_until: A feature family passes the IC sweep and the out-of-sample robustness / walk-forward battery on real data spanning more than one market regime, with no single-regime artifact, no excessive ticker concentration, and no look-ahead leakage. The model-v2 serving flag stays disabled until then.

interpretation.narrative: Phase 2L-B could not advance avg_dollar_volume_21d to model research on the current ~40-name, single-regime 2023-2026 export (NEED_MORE_DATA). Phase 2K-D therefore plans data expansion and universe broadening rather than model work: it defines the longer history, broader point-in-time universe, survivorship controls, target validation capacity, data-quality / leakage gates, and acquisition options needed before any retest. No model is trained, fitted, scored, or served, and no model candidate is created. No production edge is claimed.

recommended_next_phase.title: Expanded Historical Universe Data Feasibility Check
recommended_next_phase.purpose: Before retesting any residual signal, verify whether the required expanded dataset -- 8-10 years of daily adjusted OHLCV across a materially broader, point-in-time universe with survivorship coverage -- can actually be assembled locally / free / low-cost. The feasibility check scopes source depth, universe breadth, point-in-time membership availability, and the data-quality gates, and decides whether a paid point-in-time dataset is warranted. It acquires no paid data, trains no model, and creates no model candidate.
